column2: This workbook explores the relationship between strategic minerals, industrial sectors, manufacturing economies and national development strategies. The objective is not to estimate market value but to understand how different countries view strategic resources and how those resources support industrial capability.

Crit_Min_Frameworks - Compares national mineral strategies

01_raw_data - Source geological data

02_ref_data - Country-mineral matrix

03_global_tot - Producer counts

03_calc_demand - Scarcity / importance calculations

03_calc_weight - Country scores

Mineral Industry List - Mineral Product Sector mapping

sector-mineral matrix - Demand analysis

sector-country matrix - Manufacturing geography

sector-country list - Source company dataset

Country Code - ISO3 reference

Mineral Codes - Mineral reference

Sector Codes - Sector definitions and elasticity

Geographic
Deposit occurrence is used instead of production volume.

Industrial
Major firms are proxies for global industrial activity

Classification
Product-to-sector mapping used with engineering judgment

Strategic Frameworks
Critical mineral lists are treated as expressions of national priorities rather than objective truth.

No mid-stream data from extraction to final manufactured products

No trade flow data

No production share data

No demographic data

No value capture data
